name: Newsroom House Style Pack
purpose: Configuration for checking newsroom articles for selected, testable Guardian-style rules.

rules.rule: Spell out numbers one to nine in ordinary prose; use numerals from 10 onward, subject to the guide's exceptions.
Do not use full points in abbreviations.
rules.violation_example: The US and U.S. teams met.
rules.source: Guardian Style Guide: A — abbreviations and acronyms

rules.rule: Do not put spaces between initials.
rules.violation_example: W H Smith issued a statement.
rules.source: Guardian Style Guide: A — abbreviations and acronyms

rules.rule: Use single quotation marks for direct quotations in ordinary copy; double quotation marks may be used for words that are not actually quotations.
rules.violation_example: "The deal is done," the minister said.
rules.preferred_example: 'The deal is done,' the minister said.

rules.rule: Use double quotation marks for a quotation nested inside single quotation marks.
rules.violation_example: 'She said "yes" to the proposal,' he said.
rules.preferred_example: 'She said "yes" to the proposal,' he said.

rules.rule: Avoid 'going forward' when it is used as jargon meaning 'in the future'.
rules.violation_example: Going forward, the company will review its policy.
rules.preferred_example: In the future, the company will review its policy.
rules.source: Guardian Style Guide: G — going forward

rules.rule: Use 'obliged' rather than 'obligated' where the meaning is required or compelled.
rules.violation_example: The firm was obligated to disclose the data.
rules.preferred_example: The firm was obliged to disclose the data.

rules.rule: Avoid vague or ambiguous wording where a clearer construction is available.
rules.violation_example: The company told the regulator it had problems.
rules.preferred_example: The company told the regulator that the company had problems.
rules.source: Guardian Style Guide — clarity and usage guidance

rules.rule: Avoid 'and/or'; choose either 'and' or 'or' according to the intended meaning.
rules.violation_example: Staff can email and/or call the office.
rules.preferred_example: Staff can email or call the office.

rules.rule: Prefer precise, ordinary language over unnecessary jargon or cliché where the meaning is unchanged.
rules.violation_example: The project will leverage synergies going forward.
rules.preferred_example: The project will use the combined resources in the future.
rules.source: Guardian Style Guide — usage and jargon guidance
